key_insight: A wall-modeled fifth-order compact gas-kinetic scheme can keep outer-flow accuracy while replacing costly near-wall resolution with a pressure-gradient-aware wall model for compressible turbulent flows.
engineering_relevance: This approach enables accurate simulation of separated wall-bounded flows at much lower near-wall grid cost, making high-Reynolds-number design and analysis more practical.
method: CGKS-5th resolves the outer flow and exchanges data with a wall model at the near-wall interface.
A pressure-gradient-based non-equilibrium wall model reconstructs viscous wall stress on coarse meshes.
The model includes pressure-gradient source terms and corrected damping to handle adverse-pressure-gradient and separated regions.
evidence_signal: Validated on circular-cylinder separation and shock-induced separation on the RAE 2822 airfoil, including about 20× coarsening near the wall for the airfoil case, with improved skin-friction and separated-flow prediction.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate coupling and pressure-gradient modeling; separation physics may be sensitive in strongly non-equilibrium regions or with different mesh/interface choices.
paper_title: Efficient Wall-Modeled High-Order Compact Gas-Kinetic Scheme for Compressible Turbulent Flows
